name: Asymmetric hair part

lead: An asymmetric hair part places the parting off-centre so the hair falls in a way that balances a face whose two sides differ. The change shows as soon as the hair is styled.

Where hair falls shifts visual weight toward one side of the face, which can offset differences in brows, hairline or cheeks. It is a styling idea; research on facial symmetry covers attractiveness ratings, not hairstyle as camouflage.

paras: People try parts on different sides and at different distances from centre, often with a stylist's input, and combine them with a cut that holds the shape. It is set fresh each time you style your hair.
Risks are minimal; it is a reversible styling choice.

chain: Hair falls to offset uneven sides
angle.text: Parting hair off-centre changes where hair falls, so it offsets differences between the two sides of the face and the whole face reads as more balanced. The change is visible as soon as the hair is styled.

lead: An asymmetric hair part, in looksmaxxing usage, is an off-centre parting chosen so that hair falls in a way that visually balances differences between the two sides of the face.

Facial asymmetry is a studied subject: Wikipedia reports that greater symmetry raises attractiveness ratings and that small directional asymmetry is normal in the population [1]. It does not discuss hairstyle as camouflage.
No studies found examining the effect of hair parting on perceived asymmetry or attractiveness.

paras: No studies found. Related research on facial symmetry and attractiveness exists but does not test hair parting [1].
